info.title: Crosslane Admin REST API
info.description:
Authenticated management on the independent status HTTP listener. Model-client keys are not admin credentials. GET/HEAD permit the optional read-only token; writes require the full-access token. JSON responses use {data:...}; the OpenAPI document itself is unwrapped. Local account credentials are accepted only in write bodies and never included in account responses. Kiro Enterprise administration uses private encrypted daemon-side AWS credentials managed through crosslane admin kiro configure, with legacy CROSSLANE_KIRO_ADMIN_* environment fallback; callers send only the Admin Bearer token. Crosslane does not send separate Identity Center user or application-assignment writes. Kiro can perform application assignments internally while processing Assignment RPCs; the caller needs the downstream AWS permissions, including sso-directory:DescribeUser and sso:CreateApplicationAssignment for activation. Console control-plane protocols are not a versioned public SDK contract. Writes are submitted once and accepted responses do not prove effective access or billing. A newly created service returns its client key once. Bulk creation accepts CLI-compatible Kiro SSO CSV and returns 202 with a task URI; progress and results never contain submitted credentials.
Account control operations and service bindings resolve identities from local snapshots. Quota queries and explicit refresh/probe retain their usual upstream behavior. Service mutations preserve pending client-key edits and validate the persisted target configuration. Service writes resolve selectors within the configuration transaction. Follow-up reads reject a changed service ID instead of returning another service's data. Configuration write errors verify or restore the previous file before returning; rollback verification failures are reported explicitly.
Kiro subscription mutations/previews have eight independent operation slots and reject overlapping changes to the same resolved user. Accepted operations survive an HTTP disconnect within their AWS deadline; no automatic replay occurs. Paginated AWS collections are limited to 100 pages, 10000 items and 16 MiB in aggregate. User and membership responses must match the discovered identity store. Empty optional daemon environment values are treated as unset; STS tokens remain mandatory for temporary credentials.
Supported Identity Store user/group/store ARN references are normalized before identity checks; arbitrary resource tails are not accepted. Catchable background execution panics are reported as unknown and still produce completion audits after an HTTP disconnect.

post.summary: Create a provider-scoped account with initial tags
post.description: Tags are validated before upstream work and persisted with the new account. Kiro API-key/OAuth imports generate account and machine IDs. Kiro SSO uses the existing browser login and may take several minutes; it requires the sso build feature. Copilot tokens are verified against GitHub and Copilot before persistence, without holding the configuration lock. If hot reload replaces that provider during validation, returns 409 without saving the account; retry against the current configuration. Kiro storage errors trigger a durable-content check: a fully committed change succeeds despite stale-delta cleanup failure, while partial changes are rolled back and rollback verification failures are reported. Returns 503 immediately when all eight shared account-creation slots are occupied.

delete.description: Without force, returns 409 while any service uses this account. With force=true, unbinds every affected service (including disabled services and untagged-default/tag/manual pools), then deletes the account. Exclusions persist to protect against silent rejoining after re-import. Deletion failure restores bindings; rollback failures are reported. In-flight requests are not cancelled.

post.description: Tags can change even while services use the account; new requests recompute service pools. Untagged services only use untagged accounts, so removing the last tag moves the account into them, and adding a tag moves it out. Returns 409 when the change would leave an enabled service with no available account; set force=true to apply it anyway.

post.summary: Activate a direct Kiro USER subscription
post.description: Submits one KiroControlPlaneQDeveloperService.CreateAssignment after read-only discovery. AWS can call user-subscriptions:CreateClaim, sso-directory:DescribeUser and sso:CreateApplicationAssignment on the caller's behalf; the caller needs these downstream permissions. Existing direct claims return 409. Crosslane does not send a duplicate SSO application-assignment request or create an Identity Center user; the Kiro backend can assign the application itself. Overlapping operations for the same resolved user return 409; eight active operation slots are shared across Kiro writes/previews, with 503 on saturation. Disconnect does not cancel an already started operation. This is not an atomic compare-and-set against external AWS writers.

delete.description: Calls DeleteAssignment once. Crosslane does not delete local accounts or Identity Center users, or send a separate SSO application-assignment delete. Overlapping operations for the same resolved user return 409; eight active operation slots are shared across Kiro writes/previews, with 503 on saturation. post.summary: Upgrade a direct Kiro USER subscription
post.description: Target tier must be strictly above the unique current direct USER plan. AWS normally applies upgrades immediately. Calls UpdateAssignment once. Crosslane sends no separate SSO application-assignment write; AWS controls any application-assignment side effects. Unknown plans or ambiguous claims fail before any write. Overlapping operations for the same resolved user return 409; eight active operation slots are shared across Kiro writes/previews, with 503 on saturation. AdminBearer.description: Plaintext Admin REST token managed with crosslane admin token, or a token matching legacy digest fields. Multiple independently named admin/read-only tokens are supported. Send the plaintext value, never the stored SHA256 digest.

provider.description: Required configured provider ID. kiro driver supports api-key/oauth/sso; copilot supports token.

start_url.description: HTTPS IAM Identity Center start URL; SSO only. Maximum 8192 UTF-8 bytes.

tags.description: Alias of account_tag; send only one spelling.

providers.description: Alias of allowed_providers; send only one spelling.

force.description: Apply the change even if an enabled service would be left with no available account.

Quota.description: Unknown values remain null. Kiro totals include the configured effective overage cap. Copilot is a personal upstream quota; unlimited or zero placeholders do not establish an organization balance.

token_expires_at.description: Renewable API token deadline; null if unknown or inapplicable.

LocalAiuUsage.description: Locally observed account billing. Exact integer nano AIU; 1 AIU = 1,000,000,000 nano AIU. Independent of personal upstream quotas.

AccountGroup.description: Provider grouping includes provider_id; tag grouping includes tag (null for untagged). Multi-tag accounts appear once per tag.

uses_global_pool.description: True when the service has no account_tag. Such a service uses only untagged accounts plus manual additions, not every account.

CreatedServiceKey.description: Plaintext model-client key is returned only by service creation. Not an admin credential.

provider.description: Required configured provider ID. kiro driver supports api-key/oauth/sso; copilot supports token.

start_url.description: HTTPS IAM Identity Center start URL; SSO only. Maximum 8192 UTF-8 bytes.

BatchAccount.description: One account. Omitted provider/auth/start_url/region inherit batch defaults; tags combine with batch tags. Required authentication fields are validated after defaults are applied.

csv.description: The same email,password CSV accepted by account add --provider kiro --auth sso --batch; BOM, CRLF and quoted passwords supported.

complete.description: True only after every row succeeds.

rows.description: Input order. Present in create/show/cancel responses; omitted from list summaries.

AccountBatch.description: Process-local task report. Up to four active batches, eight concurrent REST account creations globally, 32 retained reports, finished reports retained for at most one hour. Restart clears reports and pending credentials, but preserves successfully created accounts. Cancellation stops queued rows and drains already-started logins.

dry_run.description: Perform discovery and direction validation without submitting a subscription write. Still requires a full-access Admin token.

identity_store_id.description: Canonical bare identity store ID. Equivalent ARN representations are accepted from upstream responses; foreign stores remain invalid.

principal_id.description: Canonical bare ID for recognized Identity Store user/group references. Opaque legacy group identifiers are preserved.

subscription_type.description: Raw AWS current plan name; an unknown plan remains queryable.

user_id.description: Canonical bare Identity Store UserId, even when the upstream returned an ARN.

group_subscriptions.description: All application group claims. Memberships are expanded only by the individual user subscription endpoint.
Only claims inherited through this user's current group memberships.

expected_effect.description: Expected AWS scheduling semantics, not proof that access, billing or the plan has taken effect.

application_assignment_requested.description: Whether Crosslane sent a separate SSO application-assignment request. False does not exclude application assignments performed internally by the Kiro backend.

write_outcome.description: unknown means a write may already have taken effect; query state before retrying. No automatic replay is performed.

ManagementError.description: Management error: 400 invalid input; 404 missing or disabled; 405 unsupported method; 409 conflict; 413 body limit; 500 internal error; 501 unsupported feature; 502 failed upstream action; 503 temporarily unavailable.

KiroRegion.name: region
KiroRegion.description: Kiro Profile region; overrides the active private credential configuration or legacy environment defaults. The default is us-east-1. Commercial AWS partitions only.

KiroLegacy.name: legacy
KiroLegacy.description: Explicit old control plane; only us-east-1 is supported. End-of-period cancellation is unavailable in this mode.

KiroProfileArn.name: profile_arn
KiroProfileArn.description: Defaults to CROSSLANE_KIRO_ADMIN_PROFILE_ARN, otherwise the only discovered profile; ambiguous discovery returns 409.

KiroApplicationArn.name: application_arn
KiroApplicationArn.description: Defaults to CROSSLANE_KIRO_ADMIN_APPLICATION_ARN, otherwise the only application associated with the selected profile.

KiroIdentityCenterRegion.name: identity_center_region
KiroIdentityCenterRegion.description: Optional fallback via CROSSLANE_KIRO_ADMIN_IDENTITY_CENTER_REGION when the profile lacks ssoRegion. Cannot override a different region recorded in the profile.

KiroUser.name: user
KiroUser.description: Exact Identity Center UserId (including identity-store-prefixed UUIDs), commercial AWS Identity Store user ARN, or userName. URL-encode ARN path parameters. Not a display-name search. At most 128 Unicode characters; whitespace/control characters and unsupported ARN resource types are invalid. User/store/group references are canonicalized to bare IDs before matching, and subscription writes use only bare UserIds.

KiroDeletionMode.name: mode
KiroDeletionMode.description: When to stop access. Subscription billing ends at month end in either mode; inherited group entitlements and Identity Center users/application assignments are unchanged by Crosslane.

KiroDryRun.name: dry_run
KiroDryRun.description: Validate cancellation without submitting a write.
